sources.attribution: UN DESA Population Division (2024). World Population Prospects 2024.
sources.notes: Data Portal API requires a token (HTTP 401); bulk file used. 2024+ flagged as projections.

sources.name: World Bank Population Indicators
sources.notes: Delivered within wb_wdi (SP.POP.*).

sources.name: WorldPop gridded population (1 km, UN-adjusted)
sources.attribution: WorldPop (www.worldpop.org); product DOI recorded per observation.
sources.notes: Zonal sums for each country's 4 most recent SPID survey years (2000-2024); rasters kept locally (~1.2 GB).

sources.name: BOOST public expenditure databases
sources.licence: varies by country (CC BY 4.0 / CC BY-NC 4.0 / custom)
sources.notes: Catalogue API returned HTTP 429 on every attempt; not retried with altered headers. Country files also require reviewed country-specific harmonisation.

sources.name: Government Finance Statistics — expenditure by function (COFOG)
sources.notes: Accessible without key; redistribution terms not confirmed, so values stay in the local warehouse only.

sources.name: World Bank public finance indicators
sources.notes: Flagged fiscal_comparable='national aggregates only'.

sources.name: Brazil SICONFI state accounts (DCA Anexo I-E)
sources.notes: National open-budget dataset: executed state-government expenditure by function 2015-2024; code-based geography.

sources.name: Global Data Lab — Subnational HDI and area database
sources.notes: Downloads/API require an account; not acquired without the owner's credentials. Can be added by a registered user via the same pipeline.

sources.name: UNICEF Data Warehouse (published MICS/DHS-based indicators)
sources.licence: UNICEF terms of use (reuse with attribution)
sources.notes: Open route to published MICS indicators; MICS microdata (registration) not acquired.

sources.name: UNICEF MICS microdata / subnational tabulations
sources.notes: Microdata require registration; out of scope (no restricted data on public site).

sources.name: DHS Program Indicator Data API
sources.licence: DHS Program terms (free use with citation)
sources.notes: 16 indicators with CIs and denominators; DHS region codes are survey-specific.

sources.name: Service Delivery Indicators
sources.notes: Facility-level microdata via registration; published country reports are PDFs. Not ingested.

sources.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS) Data API
sources.notes: 29 indicators incl. education spending.

sources.name: WHO Global Health Observatory
sources.notes: Non-commercial licence; uncertainty bounds kept.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap (Geofabrik extracts)
sources.notes: Open, but country extracts are 0.05-2 GB each and completeness varies; no defensible infrastructure indicator was built in this iteration. Many geoBoundaries sets are OSM-derived.

sources.name: World Bank Official Boundaries
sources.notes: Catalog API blocked (429); the AM25 boundaries matched to SPID (from the reproducibility package) are integrated instead.

sources.name: geoBoundaries (gbOpen)
sources.licence: varies by country (recorded per boundary set)
sources.notes: Used for ISO 3166-2 codes and the spatial crosswalk to SPID units.

sources.name: CHIRPS v2.0 rainfall
sources.institution: Climate Hazards Center, UC Santa Barbara
sources.notes: Annual totals 1991-2024 and anomalies vs 1991-2020.

sources.name: Global Human Settlement Layer
sources.notes: Open; deferred to keep storage within budget and because WorldPop already provides the population denominator. Degree-of-urbanisation shares are a candidate next layer.

sources.name: Travel time to cities / healthcare (Malaria Atlas Project)
sources.notes: Global ~1 km rasters (~1-3 GB); deferred within storage budget.

sources.name: ILOSTAT
sources.notes: Bulk file URLs returned empty bodies; API used.

sources.name: UNIDO INDSTAT
sources.notes: Detailed INDSTAT requires an account and restricts redistribution; a locally held copy was NOT used. WDI carries UNIDO-sourced aggregates (e.g. NV.IND.MANF.*).

sources.name: FAOSTAT Suite of Food Security Indicators
sources.notes: M49 codes mapped to ISO3 via WPP code table (code-based).

indicators.t: Mean annual rainfall of SPID area (CHIRPS v2.0)
indicators.lic: Public domain (CHIRPS); cite Funk et al. (2015)
indicators.cite: Funk, C. et al. (2015). The climate hazards infrared precipitation with stations (CHIRPS). Scientific Data 2, 150066. Climate Hazards Center, UC Santa Barbara.
indicators.def: Unweighted mean of CHIRPS 0.05° annual precipitation totals over the area.
indicators.method: Documented transformation: zonal mean over World Bank AM25 polygons (cell-centre rule; all_touched fallback for tiny polygons).
indicators.unc: Satellite-gauge blend; no per-cell uncertainty published
indicators.note: Context variable; not a welfare measure.

indicators.t: Annual rainfall anomaly vs 1991-2020 normal (CHIRPS v2.0)
indicators.lic: Public domain (CHIRPS); cite Funk et al. (2015)
indicators.cite: Funk, C. et al. (2015). The climate hazards infrared precipitation with stations (CHIRPS). Scientific Data 2, 150066. Climate Hazards Center, UC Santa Barbara.
indicators.def: 100 × (annual mean − 1991-2020 mean) / 1991-2020 mean for the same area.
indicators.method: Derived from precip_annual_mm; requires all 30 normal-period years.
indicators.unc: Satellite-gauge blend; no per-cell uncertainty published
indicators.note: Anomalies are relative to each area's own climate.

indicators.t: Married women currently using any modern method of contraception
indicators.lic: DHS Program terms of use (free use with citation)
indicators.cite: ICF. The DHS Program STATcompiler / Indicator Data API, funded by USAID. http://www.statcompiler.com
indicators.def: Percentage of currently married or in union women currently using any modern method of contraception
indicators.method: Direct estimate from a nationally representative household survey (DHS/AIS/MIS); region estimates are representative at the survey's stratification level.
indicators.unc: 95% CI where published (CILow/CIHigh); weighted and unweighted denominators in attributes

indicators.t: Energy intensity level of primary energy (MJ/$2021 PPP GDP)
indicators.def: Energy intensity level of primary energy is the ratio between energy supply and gross domestic product measured at purchasing power parity. Energy intensity is an indication of how much energy is used to produce one unit of economic output. Lower ratio indicates that less energy is used to produce one unit of output.
indicators.method: Methodology: This indicator is obtained by dividing total primary energy supply over gross domestic product measured in constant 2021 US dollars at purchasing power parity.
indicators.note: Energy intensity level is only an imperfect proxy to energy efficiency indicator and it can be affected by a number of factors not necessarily linked to pure efficiency such as climate.

indicators.cite: World Bank, World Development Indicators. Original source: Public Expenditure and Financial Accountability (PEFA), World Bank (WB), uri: https://www.pefa.org/node/5239, note: The raw data collected in order to calculate this indicator are the initially Approved and Executed Budgets. Budget Laws of countries is the usual source of the approved budget of countries. The end-of year fiscal reports (budget execution reports) are the sources of the actual spending. This data is typically obtained from websites of the Ministry of Finance (MoF) or the national Parliament, or data are collected through communication with the MoF.
indicators.def: Primary government expenditures as a proportion of original approved budget measures the extent to which aggregate budget expenditure outturn reflects the amount originally approved, as defined in government budget documentation and fiscal reports. The coverage is budgetary central government (BCG) and the time period covered is the last three completed fiscal years.

The Business Entry topic measures the process of registration and start of operations of new limited liability companies (LLCs) across three different dimensions, or pillars. The overall topic s

Methodology: B-READY is designed for benchmarking across economies. indicators.def: Progression to secondary school refers to the number of new entrants to the first grade of secondary school in a given year as a percentage of the number of students enrolled in the final grade of primary school in the previous year (minus the number of repeaters from the last grade of primary education in the given year).

indicators.note: The quality of data on the transition rate is affected when new entrants and repeaters are not correctly distinguished. Students who interrupt their studies after completing primary education could also affect data quality.

indicators.t: Mortality from CVD, cancer, diabetes or CRD between exact ages 30 and 70, female (%)
indicators.unit: Percent of females ages 30 years old
indicators.cite: World Bank, World Development Indicators. Original source: World Health Organization, Global Health Observatory Data Repository (http://apps.who.int/ghodata/)., World Health Organization (WHO), uri: https://www.who.int/data/gho
indicators.def: Mortality from CVD, cancer, diabetes or CRD is the percent of 30-year-old-people who would die before their 70th birthday from any of cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes,  or chronic respiratory disease, assuming that s/he would experience current mortality rates at every age and s/he would not die from any other cause of death (e.g., injuries or HIV/AIDS).
indicators.method: Methodology: The probability of death between the exact ages of 30 and 70 is calculated using cause-specific mortality rates for each 5-year age group, applying standard life table methods. The estimates are derived from the WHO Global Health Estimates (GHE). These estimates represent WHO's best calculations, using standard categories, definitions, and methods to ensure cross-country comparability
indicators.note:
Due to changes in input data and methods, the revisions of the data are not comparable to previously published estimates.

indicators.def: Wage and salaried workers (employees) are those workers who hold the type of jobs defined as "paid employment jobs," where the incumbents hold explicit (written or oral) or implicit employment contracts that give them a basic remuneration that is not directly dependent upon the revenue of the unit for which they work.
indicators.method:
Methodology: The proportion of wage and salaried workers to the total employed is calculated as follows: Wage and salaried workers /Total employment x 100.

indicators.def: Annual population growth rate for year t is the exponential rate of growth of midyear population from year t-1 to t, expressed as a percentage. Population is based on the de facto definition of population, which counts all residents regardless of legal status or citizenship.
indicators.method:
Methodology: The growth rate is computed using the exponential growth formula:



r = ln(pn/p0)/n, 



where r is the exponential rate of growth, ln() is the natural logarithm, pn is the end period population, p0 is the beginning period population, and n is the number of years in between. Note that this is not the geometric growth rate used to compute compound growth over discrete periods.

indicators.cite: World Bank, World Development Indicators. Original source: UCDP Battle-related Deaths Dataset , Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP), uri: https://ucdp.uu.se/downloads/, publisher: Uppsala University
indicators.def: Battle-related deaths are deaths in battle-related conflicts between warring parties in the conflict dyad (two conflict units that are parties to a conflict). Battle-related deaths refer to those deaths caused by the warring parties that can be directly related to combat. This includes battlefield fighting, guerrilla activities (e.g. hit and-run attacks/ambushes) and all kinds of bombardments of m
indicators.method: Methodology: The dataset is constructed by automatically filtering and aggregating the UCDP Georeferenced Event Dataset from the incident level to the conflict/dyad-year level, and then joining this with additional conflict-year data from related UCDP datasets. Source material is gathered in a two-pass system: first, global newswire reporting is reviewed, followed by targeted searches in local and
indicators.note: While the best estimate for battle-related deaths is considered a conservative minimum, the high estimate may still undercount actual fatalities due to unreported events, and users are cautioned that the apparent precision of the numbers does not eliminate underlying uncertainty.

indicators.t: Population of SPID area (WorldPop 1 km, zonal sum)
indicators.cite: WorldPop (www.worldpop.org), University of Southampton. Product and DOI per observation.
indicators.def: Sum of WorldPop UN-adjusted 1 km population grid cells whose centres fall in the SPID AM25 polygon.
indicators.method: Documented transformation: zonal sum of gridded population over World Bank AM25 boundaries (rasterio mask, cell-centre rule).
indicators.unc: Model-based gridded estimates; no uncertainty published at unit level
indicators.gc: within country, same product and year
indicators.fc: usable as per-capita denominator for data attributed to the same SPID units and year
indicators.note: Products differ before/after 2015 (unconstrained vs constrained); check attributes.product.
